OPENS Ch 1: ṢIRUṢAYDAN'S INTRODUCTION — the trilogy's principal-villain enters the narrative. The chapter establishes the king's Chaldean origin + idol-court + initial-violence pattern that runs through 1 Mq Ch 12 (where seed 12:11 Ṣiruṣaydan's-death narrative-climax closes the villain-arc). Per seed 11:1 (γ.4.8.B detail) the name Ṣiruṣaydan etymologizes to TYRE + SIDON (Ṣiru + Ṣaydan) per Horovitz 1905 p. 195 fn. 3 + Dillmann Lexicon Linguae Aethiopicae (1865) — making the name a TYPOLOGICAL CIPHER rather than historical-king identification. Direct biblical-typological precedents for the name-as-cipher: EZEKIEL 26-28 (Tyre-and-Sidon prophecies — the MARITIME-COMMERCIAL-PRIDE PARADIGM); ISAIAH 23 (the burden-of-Tyre oracle); JEREMIAH 25:22 + 47:4 (Tyre + Sidon in the cup-of-wrath judgment); JOEL 3:4-8 (Tyre + Sidon judgment-oracle); MATTHEW 11:21-22 par. (Christ's woe against Chorazin + Bethsaida-vs-Tyre + Sidon). The chapter's opening locates the trilogy's-villain in the canonical Hebrew-Bible enemy-typology — the king is a SYNECDOCHIC FIGURE for imperial-commercial-pride.

OPENS Ch 1 continued — COURT-SETUP narrative: Ṣiruṣaydan's idol-court is established with religious-functionaries + military-advisors + Chaldean-priests. The Meqabyan court-setup compresses the standard-biblical idolatrous-king narrative into the trilogy's opening sequence.

The chapter's first-threats establish the COVENANT-FAITHFULNESS-VS-IMPERIAL-TYRANNY framework that runs through the entire 1 Mq Ch 2-3 martyrdom-cycle. Per Horovitz 1905: the threat-pattern is structurally-identical to the LXX 2 Macc 6-7 narrative; the response (Ch 2 brothers' creation-confession) is theologically-distinct.

OPENS Ch 1 closing — TRANSITION to Ch 2 brothers' response: the chapter closes with Ṣiruṣaydan's specific tribute-demand (per seed 2:14 'Unless you bring us those warriors — THE MEQABYANS — we will burn your city with fire' — the EPONYM VERSE prepared by Ch 1's closing). The verse functions as STRUCTURAL HINGE: Ch 1's imperial-violence-setup → Ch 2's brothers'-creation-confession-and-anti-idolatry-creed → Chs 3-4 first martyrdom-cycle.

OPENS Ch 1 closing — TRANSITION to Ch 2 brothers' response: the chapter closes with Ṣiruṣaydan's specific tribute-demand (per seed 2:14 'Unless you bring us those warriors — THE MEQABYANS — we will burn your city with fire' — the EPONYM VERSE prepared by Ch 1's closing). The chapter-closing-as-transition pattern matches the trilogy's structural-method (cf. 3 Mq 1:28 chapter-closing-transition + 3 Mq 3:15 chapter-closing-transition γ.4.8.D entries). Direct biblical parallel: GENESIS 4:8-9 (the closing of Cain's first-fratricide before Abel's-blood-cries-from-the-ground); EXODUS 1:22 (Pharaoh's closing decree before Moses's birth); 1 SAMUEL 8:21-22 (Samuel's hearing the people's demand-for-a-king before Saul's anointing). The verse functions as STRUCTURAL HINGE: Ch 1's imperial-violence-setup → Ch 2's brothers'-creation-confession-and-anti-idolatry-creed → Chs 3-4 first martyrdom-cycle.
